_note: REACHED LIVE at 1440x900 through the production path, no fixture: Insert a
Text element, switch the breakpoint pill to Tablet, then centre it. That
last click is a real style write on a non-base layer, which is the only way
into this state — and it needed two new anchors to be drivable at all:
`inspector-bp-opt-<breakpoint>` on the pill's listbox rows and
`inspector-seg-<label>-<value>` on every segmented option. Both prefix-first,
for `check-anchors`'s template matcher.
MATCHES AS DRAWN, 44 properties, no drift: the header, the strip with its
three pills (the breakpoint one reading Tablet), and the whole override
molecule — the 34-tall row with its 2px accent bar, the 12/18 ink-muted
label, the 160x28 white control on a `--color/border` hairline at radius 6,
and the 32-tall accent-tint note reading 'Overridden on Tablet — Base is …'.
ONE THING CHANGED: the override row ran its own 96px label column and a 16px
right inset, which put the control at 163 against the board's 160. It now
uses `.bdi-row-ctrl`'s 95 and 20 for the reason that rule states — the board
fixes the CONTROL at 120..280 and says nothing about the label's width, so
the pixel the panel's left rule spends comes out of the label column.
AND ONE REAL DEFECT WAS FOUND HERE, fixed rather than baselined: the
type-token chain button measured 1.97:1 on HOVER — `--bk-ink` on #1E429F,
against a 3.0 floor for a 12px icon. It is a flowbite Button and carried a
bare `tw:bg-transparent`, which cannot contest flowbite's own
`enabled:hover:bg-primary-800` — a hover variant beats a base utility. The
button is only VISIBLE on hover, so the unreadable state was the only state
anyone ever saw it in. `tw:enabled:hover:bg-transparent` now.
